overview.title: 📖 Overview: The Four Blessings and Their Sources
overview.subtitle: Berakhot 48a–48b
overview.hebrewSource: וְאָכַלְתָּ וְשָׂבָעְתָּ וּבֵרַכְתָּ אֶת ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ עַל הָאָרֶץ הַטּוֹבָה אֲשֶׁר נָתַן לָךְ
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The daf finishes the question of who may be counted in a zimmun: a minor who knows to Whom we bless, and a majority who ate grain. A story about King Yannai and Shimon ben Shataḥ raises whether one who ate no bread may recite Grace for others — Rabbi Yoḥanan says no, an olive-bulk of grain is required. The Gemara then turns to Grace after Meals itself: Rav Naḥman traces each of its four blessings to Moses, Joshua, David and Solomon, and the Sages at Yavne, and a Tosefta reads all of them out of a single verse, Deuteronomy 8:10. The same verse is mined for the blessing before eating, the blessing over the Torah, and the blessing over misfortune.

slides.title: 🧒 When Does a Child Count for a Zimmun?
slides.subtitle: From 'two hairs' to a single practical test

steps.content: 1️⃣ The baraita says a minor who grew two hairs is counted, one who did not is not — and then adds 'one is not exacting with regard to a minor'. What does that clause add?
2️⃣ Answer: it includes a mature minor — one showing signs of puberty is counted, and we do not check whether he has actually reached majority
3️⃣ The Gemara rejects all of these statements: וְלֵית הִלְכְתָא כְּכׇל הָנֵי שְׁמַעְתָּתָא
4️⃣ The halakha follows Rav Naḥman: קָטָן הַיּוֹדֵעַ לְמִי מְבָרְכִין — מְזַמְּנִין עָלָיו, a minor who knows to Whom one recites a blessing is included

callout.label: Abaye and Rava as boys:
callout.text: Rabba asked them: to Whom do we bless? 'To the All-Merciful.' And where does He reside? Rava pointed to the ceiling; Abaye went outside and pointed to the sky. Rabba said: you will both be Sages — as people say, a cucumber is recognized from its blossoming stage.

slides.title: 🥬 Nine Ate Grain, One Ate Vegetables
slides.subtitle: How large a grain-eating majority does a zimmun of ten need?

lines.speaker: Rav
lines.text: If nine ate grain and one ate vegetables, they join to form a zimmun of ten. (Reported by Rav Yehuda, son of Rav Shmuel bar Sheilat.)

lines.speaker: R' Zeira
lines.text: I asked Rav Yehuda: what if eight ate grain and two ate vegetables? What if seven?

lines.speaker: Rav Yehuda
lines.text: There is no difference — they still join.

lines.speaker: R' Zeira
lines.text: Six I did not even ask about; it was clear to me that six grain-eaters are insufficient.

lines.speaker: R' Yirmeya
lines.text: You did well not to ask — but for the opposite reason! Seven or eight work because they are a majority. Six is also a majority.

lines.speaker: Gemara
lines.text: Rabbi Zeira held that we require an obvious majority (רוּבָּא דְמִינְּכַר), which six out of ten is not.

callout.label: The point of dispute:
callout.text: Everyone agrees a majority of grain-eaters is needed; Rabbi Zeira and Rabbi Yirmeya disagree only whether a bare majority of six suffices.

slides.title: 👑 Shimon ben Shataḥ at King Yannai's Table
slides.subtitle: Can someone who ate nothing recite Grace for others?

nodes.content: 🍞 King Yannai and the queen ate bread. Since Yannai had executed the Sages, no one was left to recite the blessing for them.

🤝 The queen made the king swear not to harass her guest and brought her brother Shimon ben Shataḥ, seating him between the two thrones. To the king's 'see how I honor you', he replied: it is the Torah that honors me — 'Extol her and she will exalt you' (Prov. 4:8).
🍷 Given the cup: 'How shall I bless — Blessed is He from Whom Yannai and his companions have eaten?' He drank that cup, was given another, and recited Grace.

columns.label: Rabbi Yoḥanan
columns.content: Shimon ben Shataḥ acted on his own. One cannot discharge others' obligation until he eats an olive-bulk of grain.

columns.label: Objection: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
columns.content: One who reclined with them and merely dipped in brine or ate a single dry fig joins them!

nodes.content: ✅ Resolution and halakha (Rava, via Rav Ḥana bar Yehuda): he joins for the count — even with a vegetable leaf and a cup of wine — but to discharge the many he must eat an olive-bulk of grain.

callout.label: Two different thresholds:
callout.text: Joining a zimmun requires only a token participation in the meal; leading it for others requires real bread.

slides.title: 📜 The Four Blessings: Who, When, and Where in the Verse
slides.subtitle: Rav Naḥman's history and the Tosefta's reading of Deuteronomy 8:10
headers: Hint in 'and you shall eat and be satisfied and bless…'
rows: 'The Lord your God'; Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi instead: 'Praise God with me' (Ps. 34:3)
David: 'on Israel Your people and Jerusalem Your city'; Solomon: 'on the great and holy House'
Conquest of the city; building of the Temple
'The good' — as in 'this good mountain and Lebanon' (Deut. 3:25)
HaTov veHaMeitiv — Who is good and does good
The day the slain of Beitar were brought to burial (Rav Mattana): 'good' — they did not decompose; 'does good' — they were buried
'That He gave you' (Tosefta); Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi: instituted at Yavne, no verse

callout.label: Shabbat in the third blessing:
callout.text: The baraita: on Shabbat one begins and ends the third blessing with consolation and mentions the sanctity of the day in the middle. Rabbi Eliezer allows placing it in the blessing of the land or the Yavne blessing as well; the Rabbis say only in the consolation blessing. The difference between the Rabbis and the first tanna is after the fact — the first tanna holds one who mentioned it elsewhere has fulfilled his obligation.

slides.title: 📖 One Verse, Many Blessings
slides.subtitle: The Sages extend Deuteronomy 8:10 beyond Grace after Meals

boxes.title: Blessing before eating
items: Tosefta: a fortiori — if one blesses when satisfied, all the more so when hungry
Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi: 'that He gave you' — from the moment He gave it
Rabbi Yitzḥak: 'And He will bless your bread' (Ex. 23:25) — read 'and you will bless'; it is called 'bread' before it is eaten
Rabbi Natan: the maidens told Saul the people would not eat until Samuel 'blesses the sacrifice' (I Sam. 9:13)

boxes.title: Blessing over the Torah
items: Rabbi Yishmael: a fortiori — one blesses over temporal life, all the more so over eternal life
Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Naḥmani: 'the good land that He gave [natan] you' paired with 'I will give [ve'etna] you the tablets and the Torah' (Ex. 24:12)
Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira: 'tova' is Torah — 'I have given you a good teaching' (Prov. 4:2); 'hatova' is the building of Jerusalem

boxes.title: Blessing over the bad, and required themes
items: Rabbi Meir: 'that the Lord your God gave you' — your Judge, in whatever judgment He judges you, goodness or calamity
Rabbi Eliezer: one must say 'a desirable, good, and spacious land' and mention the house of David, or he has not fulfilled his obligation
Naḥum the Elder: mention the covenant; Rabbi Yosei: mention the Torah
Pelimu: covenant before Torah, for the Torah was given with three covenants

callout.label: Why did the maidens talk so long to Saul?
callout.text: Because women are chatterers; Shmuel: to gaze longer at Saul's beauty, 'taller than the people from the shoulders up'; Rabbi Yoḥanan: because one sovereignty does not overlap its fellow even a hairbreadth — Samuel's leadership was not to be cut short.

summary.principle: A zimmun needs participants who truly share the meal, and Grace after Meals — instituted in stages by Moses, Joshua, David, Solomon, and Yavne — is rooted entirely in 'and you shall eat and be satisfied and bless'.

flowSteps.content: 🧒 Halakha per Rav Naḥman: a minor who knows to Whom we bless is counted in a zimmun
🥬 Nine (or seven, or eight) who ate grain plus vegetable-eaters form ten; Rabbi Zeira demands an obvious majority
👑 Shimon ben Shataḥ blessed after one cup — but Rabbi Yoḥanan: to discharge others, eat an olive-bulk of grain

columns.content: 📜 Moses — Hazan; Joshua — the land; David & Solomon — Jerusalem; Yavne — HaTov veHaMeitiv for the slain of Beitar
📖 Deut. 8:10 also yields the blessing before eating, over Torah, and over misfortune

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: 'And you shall eat and be satisfied and you shall bless' is the Torah source of Grace after Meals; the blessings before eating follow a fortiori — if when full, all the more so when hungry

quiz.q: According to the Gemara's conclusion, which minor is included in a zimmun?
o: Only a minor who has grown two hairs
A minor lying in a cradle
A minor who knows to Whom one recites a blessing
Any minor whose father is present
quiz.e: The Gemara rejects the earlier statements and rules like Rav Naḥman: a minor who knows to Whom we bless is counted.

quiz.q: Why did Rabbi Yirmeya say Rabbi Zeira 'did well' not to ask about six grain-eaters out of ten?
o: Because six is obviously too few to form any zimmun
Because six is still a majority, so the answer is obviously that they join
Because the question had already been decided by Rav
Because vegetables never count toward a zimmun
quiz.e: Rabbi Yirmeya reasoned that seven and eight work because they are a majority, and six is also a majority. Rabbi Zeira, by contrast, required an obvious majority and therefore considered six insufficient.

quiz.q: What does Rabbi Yoḥanan say about Shimon ben Shataḥ reciting Grace after drinking a cup of wine at King Yannai's table?
o: He acted correctly; drinking wine is enough to lead Grace
He acted on his own; one cannot discharge others' obligation without eating an olive-bulk of grain
He should not have joined the meal at all because Yannai had killed the Sages
He should have eaten a dry fig rather than drinking wine
quiz.e: Rabbi Yoḥanan holds that a token participation lets one join the zimmun, but to fulfill the obligation on behalf of others one must eat an olive-bulk of grain. Shimon ben Shataḥ's conduct was his own, not the accepted halakha.

quiz.q: Why was the blessing 'Who is good and does good' instituted at Yavne?
o: To thank God for the manna
To mark Solomon's completion of the Temple
Because the slain of Beitar did not decompose and were finally brought to burial
To commemorate Israel's entry into the land
quiz.e: Rav Mattana: on the day the slain of Beitar were brought to burial, the Sages at Yavne instituted 'Who is good' — their bodies had not decomposed — 'and does good' — they were brought to burial.

quiz.q: How does Rabbi Yishmael derive the obligation to recite a blessing over the Torah?
o: From the word 'gave' used both for the land and for the tablets
From 'tova' in 'the good land', which alludes to Torah
By a fortiori inference: if one blesses over food, which is temporal life, all the more so over Torah, which is eternal life
From the verse 'Praise God with me'
quiz.e: Rabbi Yishmael uses a kal vaḥomer from Grace after Meals. His student Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Naḥmani offers the natan/ve'etna parallel, and Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira the reading of 'tova' as Torah.
